item.text:
**Assessment:** Mostly no. I found some weak or partial pro-institution signals in 2024, but not evidence that Sisi strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, local governments, or oversight institutions when they constrained him. The year’s strongest evidence still points the other way: courts, prosecutors, security agencies, and media remained politically managed, while any reform talk was limited, reversible, or rhetorical.

**Accepted Claims**
- **President meets Prime Minister and members of the new government** | State Information Service | 2024-07-03 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/  
  Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks, improve coordination across ministries and state agencies, and emphasize integrity and transparency. This is the clearest official pro-institution statement I found, but it is general governance language, not proof of strengthened independent oversight.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.2`

- **Sisi swears in new government ministers** | State Information Service | 2024-07-03 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/  
  The reshuffle installed technocratic portfolios tied to economic management, energy, science, and foreign affairs. That suggests some reliance on formal institutions and expertise, but not independence from the presidency.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.2`

- **Egypt’s foreign ministry says it will use IAEA Board seat to strengthen nuclear safety/security and advance a Middle East nuclear-weapon-free zone** | Egypt Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-09-19 | https://www.mfa.gov.eg/ar/MediaMinistries/Details/MinistryNews/185  
  This is the strongest 2024 statement of support for a rule-bound oversight architecture, but it concerns nuclear governance rather than domestic checks on presidential power.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`

- **Human Rights Watch submission to the Universal Periodic Review of Egypt** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-15 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/15/human-rights-watch-submission-universal-periodic-review-egypt  
  HRW said some travel bans were lifted and Case 173 was announced closed, which is a limited easing of pressure on activists and NGOs. But HRW also said asset freezes and terrorism charges persisted, so this is only a partial positive.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt pardons prisoners on Police Day and January 25 Revolution** | Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS | 2024-01-25 | https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/egypt-pardons-prisoners-on-police-day-and-january-25-revolution/  
  Sisi signed a pardon covering some prisoners, including people convicted for political expression or political activity. That is a narrow relief measure, not institutional strengthening, and it does not show independent bodies gaining real leverage.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt: Civic Space Under Siege** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/egypt-civic-space-under-siege  
  HRW said authorities drastically curtailed free expression and peaceful assembly before the presidential vote to stymie meaningful competition. This is direct evidence against strengthening oversight institutions that might constrain the ruler.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt: Court Punishes Activists for Challenging al-Sisi** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-02-08 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi  
  HRW reported prison sentences and a five-year election ban for Ahmed Tantawy and supporters after peaceful political activity. This points to courts being used to entrench the executive rather than strengthened as independent constraints.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-29 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions  
  HRW reported renewed prosecutions of critics, including satirist Ashraf Omar, and said mainstream media remained severely curtailed. This is strong evidence against independent oversight of speech and media pressure.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt: Prosecutions Against Journalists and Activists Continue** | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt  
  HRW said prosecutors referred three Mada Masr journalists to trial over reporting tied to a corruption investigation. That is evidence against strengthening independent journalism and against any robust, unconstrained oversight environment.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`

- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/  
  Amnesty documented arrests of protesters and critics, plus abuse allegations and a failure to investigate properly. That cuts against any claim that oversight bodies were being strengthened to constrain coercive state power.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`, `3B.8`

- **Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-07-18 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/  
  Security forces used incommunicado detention and broad security charges after protest calls. This is evidence of coercive state machinery outranking any independent oversight function.  
  QIDs: `4B.4`, `4B.3`, `3B.8`

**Search gap**
- I did find limited reform signals, but not evidence that Sisi empowered institutions that could genuinely check him when they constrained him.
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of an independent legislature, court system, audit body, or local government gaining real autonomy.
- The positive items are best read as controlled administrative adjustments or external-facing reform language, not durable institutional independence.

**Bottom line**
- For `4B.4`, the evidence is **no**. Any strengthening was partial, tactical, or rhetorical, and it did not amount to empowering independent institutions against the ruler.
